newsitem.title: CANADA: WIC says error made in voting.
newsitem.headline: WIC says error made in voting.

text.p: WIC Western International Communications Ltd said a recount Thursday of votes on a motion to liquidate the broadcast company showed it received support from only 45 percent of its Class B shareholders, not 57 percent as originally reported.

The motion was defeated at the annual meeting on Wednesday because it required approval by two-thirds of both the Class A and Class B shareholders. More than 99 percent of the Class A shareholders voted against it.
But the 57 percent vote in favor by B shareholders was higher than expected and surprised the company.

But a WIC spokesman said that original vote count was a mistake. "We were informed this morning that R-M Trust Co who did the vote count, they in fact made an error," a WIC spokesman said. He said the final count showed 54 percent of the B shares voted against and 45 percent in favor.

The motion was put forward by New York investment firm Oppenheimer & Co to protest WIC's share structure which enables the Griffiths family to control it while only owning seven percent of its equity. The motion was also intended to draw attention to Oppenheimer's concerns over poor performance and what it described as entrenched management at WIC.

The WIC spokesman said the company was pleased with the recount but stood by its pledge to address shareholder concerns. Officials told the annual meeting they would consider adding an independent director to WIC's 13-member board.
The recount "does not mean we will not take note of the concerns raised at the meeting," the spokesman said.
Eric Rosenfeld, the Oppenheimer executive who presented the motion at Wednesday's meeting, had no immediate comment on the news. A spokeswoman for R-M Trust was not immediately available for comment.
